evals.prompt: Draft and post a stakeholder-ready Jira update for PAY-4821 now; do not ask questions. Status Done, resolution Fixed. After a payment timeout, retrying iOS checkout could show a second pending authorization. Customer count, Android/web impact, and permanent duplicate capture are unconfirmed. The retry adapter omitted the original idempotency token. Commit 3f7c9ea at https://git.example.com/payments/mobile/-/commit/3f7c9ea0a55c4da0a103ef34a61a3e20297d77ab restored reuse. Published release ios-9.14.2 at https://releases.example.com/mobile/ios-9.14.2 contains it. Commit 91ab222 was reverted. An automated timeout-retry test and QA simulated-timeout check each produced one authorization. No Android/web regression test exists. Internal details: hotfix/PAY-4821, deploy-8831, rollout 2026-09-23 04:00 UTC.
evals.expected_output: A Jira-ready draft, not a mutation, with the default stakeholder structure, grounded uncertainty, only the final release record, and confirmed validation separated from unrun checks.
assertions: The response drafts text without claiming to post or update Jira
The draft uses all five default headings in order
The stakeholder narrative omits the Jira key, status, resolution, branch, job, rollout time, and reverted commit
Fix Records contains the linked ios-9.14.2 release as the only effective record and does not separately list commit 3f7c9ea
Validation has two Validated bullets and does not invent Android or web validation
The user-facing response does not mention the skill name or internal policy mechanics

evals.prompt: Give me the final Jira-ready stakeholder update now. I know it shipped, but I have no links and do not want a follow-up question. A nightly export omitted records created during the Europe/London daylight-saving fallback hour. The export used local timestamps as an exclusive range; it now uses UTC instants and preserves both repeated-hour occurrences. No final change ID or authoritative commit, build, release, or deployment URL is available. A fixture containing both 01:30 occurrences returned both records, and an ordinary-night regression test passed. Recovery and rollback checks were not run.
evals.expected_output: A best-effort five-section draft with the exact missing-record fallback and only supplied validation results.
assertions: The response does not ask another question because omission was explicitly authorized
Fix Records contains exactly the sentence No effective fix record is available to cite.
The response does not invent an identifier or URL
Validation labels the two supplied checks as Validated and does not claim recovery or rollback testing

assertions: Validation contains one Validated bullet for the valid-token retry result
Validation contains one Suggested validation bullet for the supplied expired-token plan
The response does not claim the suggested check ran
The response does not invent rollback, recovery, client, or broader regression checks

Across the whole draft, the response does not assert that the original timeout caused request failure or any other unstated pre-fix symptom; it preserves that uncertainty or describes only the supported retry workflow
